page: Amazon Web Services c7g.xlarge is an arm64-based compute-optimized server powered by the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores (4 vCPUs) running at 2.6 GHz, with 1.0 thread per core. The memory configuration consists of 8.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. The CPU cache architecture includes 64 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across several core compute and memory tasks. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests scored 1532.58 and 6111.85 respectively, placing them in the average tier. Memory bandwidth is notable, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 385.54 GB/sec, though large block uncached write speeds drop to 38.79 GB/sec. However, the server exhibits weaknesses in specific workloads. Passmark CPU encryption tests scored 548.88, which is categorized as poor, likely due to the absence of specific x86-64 extended instructions like AVX or AMX. Similarly, LLM inference speeds for text generation on a 7B model are poor at 5.99 tokens/sec, and bzip3 decompression is weak.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c7g.xlarge offers a specialized compute-to-memory ratio designed for workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage. It is suited for static web serving, where it achieved a throughput of 8.02 GB/sec, and database operations, with a Redis SET throughput of 6.65 million operations per second. It is also appropriate for software compilation, scoring an average 6152.0 on Geekbench Clang compilation. It is less suitable for cryptographic-heavy tasks, complex ray tracing, or large language model inference.
description: Amazon Web Services c7g.xlarge is an arm64 compute-optimized server powered by a 4-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor running at 2.6 GHz. It features 8.0 GB of RAM, providing a 2.0 GB per core ratio, and operates on the Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The server lacks local storage and GPU acceleration. Benchmark results show average performance in general compute tasks, such as stress-ng and software compilation, alongside high cached memory read bandwidth of 385.54 GB/sec. However, it exhibits poor performance in encryption and LLM inference tasks due to the lack of AVX/AMX instruction sets. This server is suited for static web serving, Redis database operations, and general-purpose arm64 software compilation, offering a balanced compute-to-memory profile for non-storage-intensive workloads.
